key_insight: In simulated flash-evoked EEG, standardized Kalman methods preserve cortical activation timing more consistently than conventional Kalman filtering and LCMV beamforming.
engineering_relevance: A controlled neural-network and finite-element simulation framework supports reproducible testing of dynamic EEG source-reconstruction methods.
method: Couple a Jansen–Rit neural mass network with a realistic finite-element EEG forward model.
Simulate sequential activation across early visual, parietal, and frontal regions.
Compare SKF, change-rate SKF, conventional KF, and LCMV against known ground truth.
evidence_signal: Evaluation uses parcel-wise time courses, temporal lags, spatial focality, and Earth Mover’s Distance; change-rate SKF yields smoother temporal estimates.
watch_item: Simulation results show parcel-wise leakage and limited separation of nearby components, so temporal ordering must be interpreted alongside spatial accuracy.
paper_title: Reconstructing Flash-Evoked Potentials in the Human Brain and Tracking Cortical Activity Using Spatiotemporal Filtering: Numerical Simulation Study
